title: How stable is a refusal concept vector across light fine-tuning?

original_idea.body: Extract a refusal vector, apply several benign LoRA fine-tunes, and after each measure cosine similarity to the original direction and whether the frozen vector still steers/detects refusal.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: vector drift under fine-tuning silently breaks deployed safety layers.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: LoRA fine-tunes + re-extraction; LoRA adds a step beyond inference.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Lifecycle maintainability labs rarely publish, open models.

low_compute.reasoning: Small LoRA fine-tunes on one GPU; light training.

novelty.reasoning: Stability is a stated open problem; fine-tuning drift may be partly studied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: This refusal-vector drift framing may be open.
